answer: Divergent History Locking: each identity commits a hash-chained log of its interactions, and peers only accept new entries that extend a previously witnessed chain. A clone must replay its source's exact history, so it can never fork: any divergence invalidates the witness signatures. Like a ferrous bridge, the chain must bear identical load at every joint. An attacker pays full replication and witnessing costs per copy, and a single divergent entry collapses the whole fork. Each identity also proves liveness by signing a rotating lantern challenge;
